IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/SPECIAL CIVIL APPLICATION NO. 10723 of 2018 ==========================================================
 RAJKAMAL AGRO INDUSTRIES  Versus  DIRECTORATE OF REVENUE INTELLIGENCE ==========================================================

sentences.text:
M/S WADIAGHANDY AND CO(5679) for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MR ANKIT SHAH(6371) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 4 MR. PARTH H BHATT(6381) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 3 NOTICE SERVED BY DS(5) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1,2,5 ==========================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE ANANT S. DAVE  and  HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE BIREN VAISHNAV
Date : 27/09/2018  ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE ANANT S. DAVE)

1. The challenge in this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by the petitioner is to the arbitrary, high- handed and unreasonable action of the respondent no. 3 of detaining the goods of the petitioner without authority of law for alleged breach of the Food Safety And Standards Act vide detention memos dated 06.04.2018, 11.04.2018, 12.04.2018 and 13.04.2018 and thereafter seizure memo issued by respondent no. 2 on 19.04.2018.

1.1 The prayer clause no. 38 is basically to quash and set aside the said detention memos at Annexure 'A' collectively and also to quash and set aside seizure memo dated 19.04.2018 issued by respondents no. 3 & 2 respectively.

1.2 It is not in dispute that by communication dated 20.06.2018, respondent no. 4 imposed Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence on 27 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170662704/
1 condition of furnishing bond and undertaking upon the petitioner for provisional release of goods of petitioner weighing approximately 608 Metric Tons to which the petitioner has not responded and invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 228 of the Constitution of India.
2.

sentences.text:
Following are the contentions raised :
(I) That the petitioner is engaged in the business of importing sesame seeds from different countries which is kept in captive use, processed and then fully exported to customers outside India and that petitioner does not sell these goods in the domestic market.

It is the case of the petitioner that as per Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (for short 'FSSA') read with the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, (for short 'Licensing Regulation,
2011') earlier a license was received by the petitioner from competent authority under the FSSA, which was valid upto 17.10.2017 only.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner applied for reissue of license only on 09.01.2018 for which requisite application fees were paid by him and FSSAI ID FBO17182022305793 and Application Reference No. 10180109161540157 were generated.

(II) Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has relied on provisions of Section 110 of The Customs Act, 1962 namely seizure of goods,
documents and things which empowers the proper officer who has reason to believe that any goods are liable to confiscation under the Customs Act, seizure may be affected of the goods.

The above section according to learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner does not empower the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence authority either to seize goods or issue any seizure memo and to take further action.

Section 111(d) is in Chapter XIV of The Customs Act, 1962 which provides confiscation of any improperly imported goods and any goods which are imported and attempted to be imported or are brought within the Indian customs waters for the purpose of being imported, contrary to any prohibition imposed by or under this Act or any other law for the time being in force.
(III) Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner would contend that import of goods seized by the authority is neither in breach of The Customs Act, nor in violation of the FSSA.

Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has taken us to Section 31 of FSSA which provides for licensing and registration of food business and that no person shall commence or carry on any food business except under a licence and sub-section (4) of Section 31 which casts duty upon the Designated Officer on receipt of an application under sub-section (3) to either grant license or after giving the applicant an opportunity of being heard and for reasons to be recorded in writing, refuse to grant a license to any applicant provided he is satisfied that it is necessary to do so in the interest of public health and copy of which shall be made available to the applicant.
Section 32 is about improvement notices.

(IV) The Licensing Regulation, 2011 namely Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 framed in exercise of powers conferred by clause (o) of sub-section (2) of Section 92 read with Section 31 of Food Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence on 27 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170662704/
2 Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in detail provides for registration and licensing of food business.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Food Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Regulation 2.1.2 of the Regulations, 2011 is for license for food business and Regulation no. 2.1.3 provides for application for license to the Licensing Authority to be made in Form B of Schedule 2 to the concerned Licensing Authority.

By emphasizing Regulation No. 2.1.4 pertaining to process of application for license (clause 2 therein), it is submitted that even in case of an application which is found incomplete upon scrutiny, or if licensing authority requires any additional information with respect to the application, the licensing authority shall inform the applicant in writing to furnish such additional information or complete the application as the case may be, within 30 days from such notice and in case applicant fails to furnish the required information within the stipulated time of 30 days, the application for licensing shall stand rejected.

(V) It is averred and submitted that upon expiry of the earlier license on 17.10.2017,
the petitioner filed an application before the licensing authority on 09.01.2018 and thus the petitioner received advance authorization to import goods into India on 16.01.2018.

That the first shipment of 180 Metric Tons of sesame seeds was received from Sudan via Bill of Entry No. 5619087 at Mundra Port under Advance Import License and whole consignment was for captive use and was to be re- exported.

Further, custom authority was approached for clearance of goods from Mundra Port and NOC from the FSSAI was shown to custom officer and upon citing relevant law etc. and to ensure goods are cleared, a sample was also submitted to FSSAI for clearance.
The goods in question were tested and accordingly FSSAI issued No Objection Certificate on 28.03.2018.
Thus, certificate of custom clearance was given to the petitioner and 108 Metric Tons were released in favour of the petitioner.
Subsequently, three more consignments of the very goods i.e. Sesame seeds for the purpose of captive use and re-exporting were received for which also NOC was issued.
However, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, Ahmedabad Zone visited the premises of the petitioner along with search warrant on 06.04.2018.

entities.text: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, Ahmedabad Zone
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Though pleaded by the petitioner about no breach of any law,
detention memo was issued on 06.04.2018 itself and finally order of seizure on 19.04.2018 under Section 110(1) of The Customs Act without taking into consideration the objection of the petitioner that there was no breach of any law.
(VI) That application preferred by the petitioner on 09.01.2018 was accepted and license was issued to the petitioner by FSSAI on 27.04.2018.

It is further the case of the petitioner that till then the petitioner neither received any intimation from licensing authority about requirement of any additional information or incomplete application so mandated under Regulation no. 2.1.4.

It is submitted that various pleas were raised before respondents no. 3 and 4 stating that petitioner had Advance Import License and the goods imported are not for domestic consumption but for captive use and re- export.

(VII) Therefore, when there is no breach either under The Customs Act or under FSSA, the action of the respondents of seizure of goods and issuance of memo impugned in this petition calls for provisional release of goods unconditionally.

3 3.

entities.text: Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence on 27 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Opposing the prayers, learned Standing Counsel Mr. Parth Bhatt would contend that unless valid license for the business of food is granted to the importer or any person, no goods can be imported.

Besides, notification is issued under The Customs Act, 1962 in exercise of powers conferred under sub-section (1) of Section 4 of The Customs Act, 1962, the Principal Director General of Revenue Intelligence, New Delhi or Director General of Revenue Intelligence to be the Principal Chief Commissioner of Customs or Chief Commissioner of Customs who shall have jurisdiction over the whole of India.

In addition to above, even disputed jurisdiction, if any, can also be gone into at the later stage of adjudication provided the petitioner is ready and willing to comply with the conditional order for provisional release of the goods.
The above release order is passed after considering the Board Circular dated 16.08.2017 and bank guarantee of 20% for the provisional release of the seized goods is ordered.

Reference is made to Section 2(33) of Customs Act i.e.
"prohibited goods", provisions of Section 111(d) of the very Act.

Considering the nature of goods imported by the petitioner, in absence of a valid license, having assessable value of Rs.4,53,48,752/-
covered under various four Bills of Entries, panchnamas while detaining the goods and communication addressed by Senior Intelligence Officer, DRI, Ahmedabad to Food Safety and Standard Authority of India and reply received reveal that license application receipt sent by the applicant does not exist in their system and is not genuine.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, the Court exercising jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India would be loath in interfering with the order passed for provisional release of seized goods upon imposing of conditions and only 20% of bank guarantee is given subject to rights and contentions of the parties.

3.1 Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent authority invite various pleadings filed in this petition to which learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner reiterated that receipt produced was neither fake nor tampered with and affidavit filed by the Consultant of the applicant dated 08.09.2018 along with statement of account of State Bank of India reveal that application fees of Rs.37,970.45 was shown in the debit column.
That due to any technical error etc.

if it is not reflected in online application, the applicant is not at all at fault and therefore the order impugned is inherently without any jurisdiction as well as contrary to law and prayer be allowed by setting aside the impugned orders.
4.

At the outset, we are of the view that though application was preferred for renewal of license by the applicant on 09.01.2018 upon license issued earlier expiring on 17.10.2017 and NOC etc. issued by the competent authority under FSSA for the relevant consignment, the fact remains that application for reissuance of license was accepted only on 27.04.2018.
In a case of incomplete application or the requirement of the authority to furnish additional information or any lacuna, such officer ordinarily ought to have intimated the applicant.
But in the facts of this case, the very dispute is raised about receipt of application with requisite fees.

Under the circumstance, so long as valid license was not issued in favour of the petitioner, irrespective of any clearance given by FSSAI authorities on basis of which clearance was given by customs authority, action of the petitioner amounts to be one contrary to law and not that of the authority.

5. The panchnama drawn on 06.04.2018 reveals the following aspects:

sentences.text:
"Officers also find that total 3600 bags (180 MTS) packed in HDPE bags on which sticker are affixed with the details of name of the product-Reddish Sesame Seeds,
Crop year - 2017-2018, Country of Origin - Sudan, Packing Date - January-2018,
Expiry Date - January-2020, Net Weight - 50.10 kgs are also lying in the factory premises but they are not mentioned in the stock List.

On being asked about it, Shri Manish Khatri informs that as he already informs in the above para that siad goods are those which were imported under Bill of Entry No. 5619087 dated 17.03.2018 but not make entry in the stock list.

Thereafter officer asks Shri Ratan Lal Agarwal whether they possess licence required for the import of sesame seeds as required under Food Safety and standards (Imports) Regulation, 2017, Shri Ratan Lal Agarwal informs the officer that they do not possess the said license and they have cleared the said imported goods without the said license from Customs, Mundra.

The officers informs Shri Ratan Lal Agarwal that as per the said regulation no person shall import any article of food without any import license from the Central Licensing Authority in accordance with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Shri Ratan Lal Agarwal informs the officer that the said 3600 bags (180 MTS) of sesame seeds were imported by them under Bill of Entry No. 5619087 dated 17.03.2018 without license from the Central Licensing Authority.

The officers informs Shri Rathan Lal Agarwal in our presence that the said import without license is in contravention of the Food Safety and Standars (Imports) Regulation, 2017 which resulted in contravention of the provisions of Customs Act, 1962.

Therefore the officer detains the said goods today on 06.04.2018 having assessable value Rs.13662732/- under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962 and handover it to Shri Ratan Lal Agarwal under Supratnama dated 06.04.2018 for the safe custody of it."
6. Considering the above and also the notification issued by the Board under the Customs Act empowering Principal Director General of Revenue Intelligence, New Delhi or Director General of Revenue Intelligence to be the Principal Chief Commissioner of Customs and Chief Commissioner of Customs, it cannot be said that the action of the respondents is without authority and therefore seizure order is illegal.
On the very short ground as above, we are not inclined to interfere with the order passed.
However, this order may not come in the way of the petitioner if the petitioner is ready and willing to comply with conditional provisional release order.
Petition is dismissed.
Notice is discharged.
Interim relief, if any, shall stand vacated.
(ANANT S. DAVE, J) (BIREN VAISHNAV, J)
